purpose.primary: Define a minimal, voluntary learner feedback mechanism that remains separate from learning, mastery, badges, identity, and behavioral analytics.
purpose.concept: Allow a learner to leave a small voluntary trace of their learning experience without requiring a public profile or unnecessary identifying information.
purpose.metaphor: A small note left on a community corkboard rather than a learner account or social profile.

core_principle: A learner may quietly say, "I was here, and this was my experience," without being required to identify themselves.

learning_separation.principle: Feedback should never become the price of completion.

fields.label: Where are you learning from?
fields.purpose: Allow the learner to voluntarily associate a broad location with the learning experience.

fields.label: One thought about your experience
fields.purpose: Allow the learner to leave a brief voluntary reflection about the learning experience.

country_boundary.reason: The Footprint concerns the broad location the learner voluntarily associates with the learning experience, not nationality, birthplace, ancestry, citizenship, or family background.

reflection_boundary.purpose: Capture one small voluntary learning reflection rather than create a comment system or biography.
reflection_boundary.reminder: Please do not include personal or identifying information in your reflection.

data_minimization.principle: If the Footprint can work without knowing something about the learner, prefer not knowing it.
data_minimization.rule: Do not collect tomorrow's data today.

not_a_profile.principle: A Footprint is a voluntary contribution, not a learner identity.

not_analytics.principle: Curiosity about learners does not automatically justify observing them.

do_not_infer: learner refused participation for a particular reason

interpretation_boundary.a_submitted_footprint_supports: A Footprint was voluntarily submitted containing the fields actually provided.
does_not_support: the submitted country represents the learner's nationality or origin
absence of a Footprint indicates non-completion
interpretation_boundary.principle: Do not upgrade voluntary Footprint data into claims about the full learner population.

badge_separation.badge_meaning: The learner completed the Guide and demonstrated its defined skill.
badge_separation.footprint_meaning: The learner voluntarily chose to leave a small piece of feedback.
badge_separation.principle: A Footprint adds no academic status to a badge.

prefer: broad location only when voluntarily supplied
public_display.principle: Public Footprints should remain a collection of voluntary traces rather than become a scoreboard.

small_group_risk.principle: Broad information can become identifying when only a small number of people match it.
small_group_risk.default_response: Prefer less public precision when additional detail could make a contributor easier to identify.

shadow_profile_boundary.principle: Individually minor fields can become identifying when combined.
shadow_profile_boundary.warning: A set of individually harmless details may become a behavioral or identifying profile when joined.

free_text_safety.risk: A learner may accidentally include personal or identifying information in a reflection.
free_text_safety.learner_reminder: Please do not include personal or identifying information in your reflection.
free_text_safety.principle: Voluntary submission does not mean every submitted detail must automatically become public.

consent_design.principle: Consent works best when no is easy.

example_interface.title: Leave a Footprint
example_interface.notice: Please do not include personal or identifying information in your reflection.
example_interface.action_priority: Both options should be easy to access.

example_submissions.reflection: The second observation exercise made me notice how much I was filling in myself.
I finally understood why uncertainty can be useful.

retention_and_control.principle: Voluntary participation should not become irreversible merely because someone submitted once.

technical_data_boundary.do_not_claim: No information ever reaches a server.
technical_data_boundary.reason: Actual technical request handling depends on the eventual architecture, hosting environment, logging, and security configuration.
technical_data_boundary.design_commitment: Do not intentionally build unnecessary identity, behavioral tracking, or profiling into the Footprint system.
technical_data_boundary.future_requirement: Document actual technical behavior when an implementation exists.

do_not_infer: implementation details not present in the source

awareness.question: What information are we actually collecting?

alignment.question: Does each collected element correspond to a real need?
alignment.rule: Remove information that has no clear purpose.

coherence.question: Does the implementation match the privacy promise?
coherence.rule: Do not allow learner-facing privacy language and actual system behavior to diverge.

clarity.question: Can an ordinary learner understand what happens when a Footprint is submitted?
clarity.rule: Prefer plain descriptions of actual behavior.

continuity.question: If the system changes later, does the privacy promise still hold?
continuity.rule: Reinspect the privacy model when implementation changes.

when_presenting_footprint: Treat the learner's submitted country as self-selected location information only.
Remind the learner not to include identifying information in free text.
Offer an equally accessible continue-without-submitting path.
when_interpreting_footprints: Describe only what was voluntarily submitted.
Do not infer nationality or origin from country.
Do not infer non-completion from absence.
Do not use voluntary Footprints as a proxy for all learners.
must_not: treat feedback as a mastery requirement
treat a Footprint as proof of overall learner demographics
